g.text: Your Poster Title Goes Here: A Concise, Descriptive Statement of Your
Department of —, Institution Name, City, Country ·
Department of —, Institution Name, City, Country
Replace this text with your introduction. State the context of your
research, the problem you address, and why it matters for sustainability
and the circular economy. Two to four short paragraphs read best at
Keep sentences short. Viewers typically read a poster from two metres
away, so favour clear statements over dense prose, and let ﬁgures carry
State your ﬁrst research objective in a single clear sentence.
State your second objective —what you measured, built, or modelled.
State your third objective —the intended outcome or impact.
Optional fourth objective; remove items you do not need.
Summarise your experimental design, materials, computational approach,
or analytical framework. Reference your process diagram below rather
than describing every step in text.
State sample sizes, instruments, software and statistical methods brieﬂy
—reviewers and delegates look for them here.
Present your principal ﬁndings. Lead with the headline result, then
support it with the ﬁgures and table below. Every ﬁgure should be
readable on its own, with units on every axis.
Key quantitative result with conﬁdence intervals.
Interpret your results here. What do they mean, how do they compare with
prior work, and what are the limitations? Keep it to the few points a viewer
First conclusion —the single most important ﬁnding of this work.
Second conclusion —the supporting result or implication.
Third conclusion —relevance to circularity, energy or environment.
Outline the next steps: planned experiments, scale-up, deployment
pathways, or open questions inviting collaboration with the SustainX
Acknowledge funding agencies, grant numbers, collaborators, and facilities here. Example: This work
Hide this panel from the toolbar before exporting your final poster.
Process diagram / schematic · export as SVGfrom Draw.io, Figma, Illustrator, Visio or PowerPoint ·
Export from Origin, MATLAB, Python, R, Prism, SigmaPlot or Excel as SVG—never a screenshot ·
recommended ≈ 240 ×160 mm · axis labels & legends ≥ 18 pt
Chemical structures & mechanisms · export as SVGfrom ChemDraw or equivalent —avoid raster
Micrograph, photo or rendered ﬁgure · raster images ≥ 300 DPI and ≥ 2500 px wide · vector (SVG)
Use this callout for your single headline takeaway — the one sentence you
want every SustainX delegate to remember.
Author, A. et al. Title of the article.
Author, B. & Author, C. Title of the article.
Author, D. et al. Title of the article.
Export Origin, MATLAB, Python, R, Prism, SigmaPlot & Excel plots as SVG.
Build ﬂowcharts in Draw.io, Figma, Illustrator, Visio or PowerPoint.
Avoid raster exports of line art.
PDF: high-quality print, no compression, never “minimum ﬁle size”.
Zoom to 400–500% —verify text and graphs stay sharp.
